title: Day 96: Michoacán AG Confirms 60+ CJNG Colombian Mercenaries in Purépecha Plateau; Plan Kukulkan 13 Days; El Sapo Still at Large
detail: Day 96 since El Mencho's killing at Tapalpa, Jalisco (February 22, 2026). CJNG COLOMBIAN MERCENARIES — PURÉPECHA PLATEAU CONFIRMED (Day 96): Michoacán's state attorney general (FGE Michoacán) formally confirmed that more than 60 Colombian paramilitary operatives are embedded with CJNG forces currently conducting an offensive across the Purépecha indigenous highlands of Michoacán. The cell operates in 8–10 pickup trucks and is contesting the Ciénega de Zacapu / Purépecha Plateau corridor against the Los Reyes Cartel and remnants of the Knights Templar. The FGE linked CJNG and the Colombian operatives to ongoing attacks in at least 10 Michoacán municipalities: Zamora, Jacona, Tangamandapio, Tangancícuaro, Chilchota, Charapan, Paracho, Cherán, Nahuatzen, and Los Reyes. The mercenaries' stated objective is to consolidate a corridor dominating the Canyon of the Eleven Pueblos and the Sierra de los Reyes — areas prized for logging, mineral extraction, and drug transit routes to the Pacific. Recent confirmed incidents in the Purépecha theater: (May 20) Security forces killed 3 CJNG gunmen on the Cocucho–Ocumicho road in Hidalgo Norte municipality. (May 17) Gunmen attacked a Community Police barricade in Sevina, Nahuatzen — 2 community police officers killed. The presence of Colombian paramilitaries within a CJNG offensive is consistent with broader documented patterns: CJNG imported Colombian and Guatemalan former combatants for El Sapo's personal security detail, and the cartel has used foreign tactical specialists since at least 2021. The Purépecha highlands deployment adds a third active CJNG indigenous-community front in Michoacán: the Aquila coastal corridor (7+ attacks on Nahua communities May 19–22), the Tierra Caliente perennial conflict zone (ongoing), and now the Purépecha Plateau. This is the most significant escalation of CJNG offensive operations in Michoacán's highland zones since the post-Mencho succession crisis began 96 days ago. PLAN KUKULKAN — 13 DAYS: Thirteen days remain before the FIFA World Cup 2026 opening match (June 11, Estadio Azteca, Mexico City vs. South Africa). Defense Secretariat (SEDENA) confirmed on May 27 that Plan Kukulkan is proceeding as planned. Forces deployed: 99,000+ total — 20,000 Armed Forces, 55,000 federal/state police, 188 canine units, 2,100 military vehicles, 24 aircraft and drones. Guadalajara's Akron Stadium (4 group-stage matches) remains under heightened CJNG-specific protocols. U.S. special forces continue training Mexican military on stadium attack prevention and drone bomb defense. EL SAPO HUNT — DAY 96: Hugo Gonzalo Mendoza Gaytán ('El Sapo' / 'El 090') remains at large as Mexico's #1 CJNG enforcement target — no capture or elimination reported. El Sapo's capture or elimination before June 11 remains Mexico's Federal Security Cabinet's stated top CJNG objective. MANZANILLO COMMAND VOID — DAY 20: Twenty days since El Chucky's arrest (May 9); no confirmed successor plaza boss for the Port of Manzanillo — Mexico's primary fentanyl precursor entry point. SUCCESSION BINARY: El 03 (Juan Carlos Valencia González — confirmed leader, financial wing) vs. El Sapo (military wing, at large). CIAGATE FGR INVESTIGATION (Day 96): Ongoing — 'coordination without subordination' Mullin-Sheinbaum framework active; June bilateral security meeting scheduled. DECAPITATION LEDGER — DAY 96: El Mencho (killed Feb 22), El Tuli (killed Feb 22), El Doble R (arrested Mar 11), El Jardinero (arrested Apr 27; extradition suspended), El Güero Conta (arrested Apr 27), El Chipo/Jorge N (arrested May 19), El Cabo (arrested May 7), El Chucky/Manzanillo (arrested May 9), El Checo/Tecate (arrested May 13). Operativo Enjambre: 80+ officials. 47+ CJNG HVTs neutralized since Feb 22.

media.caption: CJNG deploys 60+ Colombian paramilitary operatives in Michoacán's Purépecha Plateau — Michoacán AG formally confirms presence across 10 municipalities
